svg.text: Fux, in detail
Every plane, what is committed and what is not, the two query paths, and the two readers.
committed -- belongs in git
derived -- rebuildable, gitignored
acquired -- gitignored, NOT rebuildable; the refer plane
off by default, or not built
1 - SOURCES -- WHAT COUNTS AS A DOCUMENT
.fuxignore
Read FIRST and outranks the lists.
.gitignore grammar; last match wins.
Nothing in formats.toml subtracts.
formats.toml
include = [...] globs
[decoders] ext -> module, [meta] bindings
Absent = the built-in default.
sources/dirs
One directory per line.
A leading ! excludes.
archived=true marks retired.
sources/urls
One URL per line: fetch= decoder=
keep= ttl= update=. Routed to YOUR
fetcher; there is no default fetcher.
2 - INGEST -- THE ONLY PATH INTO THE COMMITTED PLANE
walk / fetch
git dir walk, or your
fetcher, resolved per
line: pin > route >
ROUTES claim (W-199)
decode
17 built-ins; your
.fux/decoders/ copies
are what run. Nothing
readable -> the queue
content_sha
blake2b-160 ON THE
RAW BYTES, before
redaction.
Load-bearing.
redact
pii.toml, REQUIRED.
Body + frontmatter
title. Not the path.
Only the committed side.
extract
title, phrases, terms
+ flen over 5 fields,
abbr pairs, identifier
families (W-233)
edges
Re-resolved EVERY run:
ref, tag, code,
supersedes; a ref
carries anchor hashes
write
superseded + mtime
stamped as facts;
shards + REGISTER;
then fux build runs
decode() returned nothing -> a row in .fux/enrich/queue.tsv with the reason. Queued, never dropped -- "no decoder for X" becomes a doctor row; "nothing readable" is fux enrich's worklist (W-248).

Delta ingest: an unchanged sha reuses its extraction verbatim, byte-identical to --full. The reuse key also watches pii.toml, the [index] caps, identifiers.toml, each decoder and each enrichment file --
any of them moving re-extracts what it touched. Edges are never reused. Bytes reach a shard through ONE call, write_index; a stopped run never leaves a partial shard.
3 - THE COMMITTED PLANE -- THIS IS THE PRODUCT
.fux/index/
256 shards, {00..ff}.jsonl, one canonical JSON line per document. Doc-major, sorted keys, so it diffs like code. Shard = blake2b(doc id, 1 byte).
Line 1 of every shard is a header: _format fux.index.v7 - analyzer v3 - tf_fields - the identifiers digest, only when families exist. REGISTER sits beside the shards:
loc kind sha decoder fetcher, one line per document, sorted, no clock (W-199). A bundled git merge driver (fux-merge-index) handles two branches touching the index.
id / src / loc
file:docs/x.md or url:https://...; src is git or url
terms
hash -> per-field counts, 5 fields, zeros omitted
flen
field lengths; wlen is DERIVED at query time
title / phrases
display only -- the max_phrases cap never touches ranking
sha
of the RAW bytes -- what answer verifies against
mtime
git commit time. Recency never reads a clock.
edges
kind + dst + grade; a ref adds at/al, anchor hashes
abbr
hashed Long Form (ABBR) pairs the text itself declares
ver / mode
ver bumps on a sha change; mode: extracted
archived / superseded
facts, absent when false; tie-breaks, never weights
Gone since v4 (W-194)
meta and title_h -- ex-L5's hashed display fields
Never committed
df, avg_wlen, the mined table, the anchor fold: all read-time
No content. Ever. The index holds statistics about your documents and never the documents -- that is L3, and it is why there is no second copy to go stale.
Committed beside the index
pii.toml
REQUIRED -- every verb but setup, tune,
output and doctor refuses without it
tune.toml
ORDERING only -- except [index], which caps what
is indexed. Every key required, none in code (L12)
output.toml
SHAPE only -- how a result is shown,
never which documents come back
identifiers.toml
ID families kept whole (RF-118 = rf118). CHANGES
THE INDEX; its digest is in every shard header
refusals.toml
what a sign-in wall or paywall looks like here.
Consumer-owned; fux ships no vendor knowledge
inspect.toml
the knobs of fux inspect's lenses and floors --
what the report flags, never what is ranked

also committed: sources/ fetchers/ decoders/ observers/ enrich/ node/ fux (the shim) formats.toml .fuxignore README.md .gitignore -- every entry is declared in store/fuxdir.py; fux doctor warns on anything else.
4 - THE TWO GITIGNORED PLANES -- AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING
.fux/runtime/ -- DERIVED
fux build -- Python's, or Node's since 2026-10-03 -- rebuilds the accelerator from the shards alone:
postings/ anchors/ docs.jsonl stats.json mined.json graph.json
manifest.json stamp.json
Per-machine state lives beside it, local and gitignored, and no build rewrites it:
fetch-cache/ dirty write.lock url-state.json pii-digest decoder-digests.json
ingest-log.jsonl provenance.jsonl (--journal) inspect/ trace/ enrich-progress.tsv
Safe to delete, any time. Carries CACHEDIR.TAG, so backup tools skip it unasked. ingest rebuilds it.
.fux/acquired/ -- ACQUIRED
The bytes a fetch actually returned, for URLs whose line says keep=true -- the
DEFAULT; keep=false opts out. Bounded by [sources.url] acquired_max_bytes.
objects/<sha256> plus a manifest.json that lives HERE, never on the record.
Gitignored and tagged like derived -- but NOT rebuildable.
Deleting it loses the only local copy. Getting it back means re-fetching from
a source that must still exist and a session that must still hold.
A third kind, not a subdivision of derived. It turns an unreachable URL's unverified into as-ingested.
.fux/.gitignore lists the ignored directories BY NAME and never a wildcard: runtime/ acquired/ __pycache__/ node/node_modules/ index/*.jsonl.tmp.
One .fux/* line would quietly drop the committed index from git with no error -- so fux doctor asserts this against git check-ignore itself.
5 - QUERY -- EVERY CALL, AND THE LAW THAT LETS THERE BE TWO PATHS
Reference scan -- the default
Read every shard as raw bytes; parse a line only when it substring-matches
a query hash. No build step: a fresh clone answers, slower.
Accelerator -- only with --fast, only if fresh
Rarest-first, block-max bound, rounding-aware skip test over runtime/. Falls
back to the scan when the stamp no longer matches -- and says so on stderr.
The differential law
Accelerator results EQUAL reference-scan results.
Float addition is not associative, so the accelerator never accumulates
a score. It produces candidates and statistics; rank() does every
arithmetic operation, once, for both. Asserted by tools/differential/.
--fast can only ever change speed. That is asserted, not hoped.
rank()
expansion guard -> BM25F over 5 committed fields + anchor, folded in at read time -> x [priority] x intent prior -> the declared 5-key sort -> ties marked before truncation
body 1.0 heading 3.0 title 2.0 path 1.5 ctx 1.0 anchor 1.0 k1 1.2 b 0.15 (measured, W-144) sort: (-round(score,9), superseded, -mtime, -priority, id)

Inside the core: mined expansion 0.5 (abbreviations the corpus declares) and the intent prior 0.1 (needs a [doctype] table). After it: proximity rerank (OFF) - a human pin (fux correct) - the graph tier,
RRF of lexical and PPR (ON) - the band. -q arms are fused by RRF at k=60. archived_weight, superseded_weight, recency and RM3 are gone; superseded and mtime reach the order only as tie-breaks.
6 - REFER -- THE ONLY PART THAT LEAVES THE MACHINE
fux answer ranks top-3 (constants.toml [answer] candidates), then goes and reads the source before it quotes.
file: reads the checkout, decoded by the same decoders - url: the TTL fetch cache, else your fetcher under a hard timeout, else .fux/acquired/, else it says it did not look.
current - stale - cached - as-ingested - unverified
Then: chunk on headings (frontmatter is passage 0; transient, never written) -> rescore with the same BM25F over the passage set -> assemble under 8000 bytes -> cite a line range and a fresh sha.
A url: whose sha differs is marked dirty, and the next ingest re-fetches only those lines. fetch_at_answer = true by default; ttl= on the line (24h) bounds how long a citation goes unchecked.
sha
differs
url
marked
dirty
a narrowed
re-ingest
fixes
ranking
7 - THE TWO READERS -- ONE INDEX, ONE CONTRACT, AND A THIRD ARM OF THE LAW
python -- fux-engine 3.0.0-alpha.10 on PyPI
Every verb (24), and the only thing that ingests: setup doctor inspect identifiers - ingest build -
add remove enrich correct - ask find answer lexical - explain graph path - serve mcp daemon -
hooks tune output verify. Reference scan by default; the accelerator with --fast.
from fux import open -> ix.find / ask / answer / explain / graph / path
dependencies = [] (L2). Python >= 3.12 (L7). Library and CLI render one payload (W-247).
node -- fux-engine on npm, vendored to .fux/node/
ONE bundled fux.mjs (53 authored modules) + package.json, mcp-tools.json, README.md -- no build
step FOR YOU (L10). COMMITTED, rewritten at the head of every ingest when the engine version differs.
.fux/fux -> the bundle, else node_modules/.bin, else an ancestor's bin
find ask answer explain graph path mcp build (--fast / --scan)
Reads runtime/ under --fast and on mcp; fux build is its ONE write (W-242, 2026-10-03). Node >= 22 (L8).
The differential law, third arm: python == node -- same ids, same order, same locators and band. The printed score is equal after round(9); the ORDER has no tolerance at all.
Four asymmetries are decisions, not gaps: Node never fetches, so url: is never current or cached (it reads .fux/acquired/, or declines) - it reads a fresh graph.json and rebuilds in memory
otherwise (W-259), so it never requires fux build - markdown is its only decoder, so it declines what it cannot decode - verify, --why, --receipt and --journal are out of scope on this reader.
8 - THE LAWS THIS SHAPE EXISTS TO SATISFY (HANDLES AS RENUMBERED 2026-09-28)
L2
$0 and FOSS-only
dependencies = [] today. The zero-dependency guarantee was withdrawn 2026-09-06; a runtime dependency now needs an OSI licence AND an accepted record.
L3
content is never durable
The index holds statistics; link text and abbreviations go in as hashes. Chunks are re-derived transiently at answer time and written nowhere.
L4
deterministic
Same sources, byte-identical index -- and REGISTER, and the runtime plane from either builder. No wall clock, no filesystem order, no model.
L5
offline by default
ask and find never touch the network. Only ingest and answer can, and only through your fetcher; an import fence test enforces it.
L9
a use record is never committed
The --journal log, the dirty list and every trace of a question live under gitignored runtime/. REGISTER names documents, never a reader.
build output, never source
The consumer gets ONE bundled fux.mjs; the only readable source in their tree is their own .fux/decoders/ and .fux/fetchers/.
every value lives in config
Tunables in .fux/*.toml and fux.toml; fixed values in src/fux/constants.toml, read by both planes. A missing key is a hard error naming it.
ex-L5
hashed meta (retired)
Deleted 2026-09-20 (W-194) with meta and title_h; the ACL-mismatch leak it closed is an accepted exposure. Was L5 before the renumber.

The rest of the thirteen: L0 the records are the only source of truth - L1 a retired record is archived, never deleted - L6 say index, not db - L7 Python >= 3.12 - L8 Node >= 22 - L11 the golden answer key is sealed (W-234).
Not built, and named here so no one reads it off a diagram as shipped:
the paper's single content-addressed MST keyspace (L/ P/ D/ V/ E/ M/) -- what shipped is flat sharded JSONL. The dense / vector lane -- deleted 2026-08-25, and the V/ plane with it.
The ARC cache (refer/arc.py) is implemented and tested but never constructed on any CLI path -- the cache that actually runs is the TTL fetch cache under .fux/runtime/.
The enriched ingest MODE: SR-ENRICH ratifies the name and the record shape, not the build (W-263 researches it). Sections as records: SR-SECTIONS is proposed, not in the index (W-236).
Drawn from the code, 2026-10-05. src/fux/store/, src/fux/ingest/, src/fux/derive/, src/fux/query/, src/fux/refer/, src/fux/constants.toml, src/fux/templates/tune.toml.txt, node/src/, CHANGELOG.md.

SR-DOTFUX (0102) - SR-RECORD (0109) - SR-INGEST (0106) - SR-REFER (0127) - SR-ACQUIRED (0145) - SR-NODE-SEARCH (0153) - SR-LAWS (0001). Overview: architecture-high-level.svg. Readers: architecture-two-readers.svg.
